transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Thank you for seeing me, doctor. When I start eating, especially in the evenings, I feel like I lose control and can’t seem to stop myself. It has become incredibly difficult to manage on my own, and I'm quite embarrassed to even admit it.

After these episodes of feeling unable to stop eating, do you ever try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? Or are the episodes mainly the loss of control without those behaviors?

I'm deeply ashamed to admit it, but yes, I do try to make up for it in those ways. Sometimes I'll sneak into the bathroom to make myself throw up or take extra laxatives, while other times I'll starve myself the next day and force myself onto the treadmill until my knees ache. I just feel this desperate need to erase the damage and get back on track.
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you feel about yourself? Are you very afraid of gaining weight even when your weight is normal?

My weight and shape completely dictate how I feel about myself, and if the scale goes up by even two pounds, I panic and obsessively replay everything I've eaten. Even though my doctors say my weight is fine, I am absolutely terrified of getting fat. I just constantly dread the thought of people at my church or my office judging me for it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of loss-of-control eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, and excessive exercise. Self-evaluation is overly influenced by body weight/shape, and there is intense fear of weight gain despite normal weight. This pattern is most consistent with bulimia nervosa.
